questionReview.question: Which principle best characterizes consistent dietary vitamin K?
choices: Consistent vitamin K intake is safer than eliminating nutritious vitamin K-containing foods.
A stable INR requires complete avoidance of all vitamin K-containing foods.
A low-vitamin-K enteral formula rules out any interaction with warfarin.
Water flushing alone prevents warfarin from interacting with enteral feeding.
questionReview.rationale: Maintain a consistent vitamin K pattern and review nutrition products for vitamin K content. Enteral products may also bind warfarin; formula vitamin K content alone does not explain every low INR.
questionReview.review: The retained consistency principle is supported by517/523. All three distractors now test incorrect avoidance, low-vitamin-K immunity or flush-only handling rather than unrelated true principles.

questionReview.question: Which clinical action best applies to consistent dietary vitamin K?
choices: Teach patients to maintain a stable pattern and report major dietary, supplement, or nutrition-support changes.
Eliminate leafy vegetables rather than establish a consistent intake.
Keep the same INR follow-up plan after major nutrition changes because the prior INR was stable.
Use the vitamin K content alone to decide whether warfarin can be given during continuous feeds.
questionReview.rationale: Consistency and communication allow the anticoagulation plan to account for nutrition changes. Check supplements and formula vitamin K content, and coordinate administration when enteral feeding can reduce warfarin effect.
questionReview.review: Keep consistent intake and communicate changes. Each new distractor either imposes avoidance, fails to reassess a major change or treats formula vitamin K as the whole interaction.

questionReview.question: Which assessment is most appropriate for consistent dietary vitamin K?
choices: Review greens, oils, nutrition shakes, enteral feeds, supplements, appetite, weight loss, diarrhea, alcohol, and INR trend.
Review only green vegetables and assume nutrition shakes, feeds and supplements have no vitamin K.
Review formula vitamin K content but exclude the actual warfarin administration and feeding schedule.
Review only the prescribed dose and prior INR, without asking what nutrition products changed.
questionReview.rationale: Review the overall intake and INR trend, including nutrition products and supplements. Enteral formulas vary in vitamin K content and can bind warfarin, so assess both vitamin K exposure and actual drug-feed delivery. Changes in intake warrant communication and INR reassessment.
questionReview.review: Complete dietary/nutrition review is better than the three explicitly incomplete assessments.517 identifies foods/oils, supplements and EN vitamin K;170 establishes binding and actual drug-feed timing;516 establishes nutrition-sensitive dosing/INR monitoring;523 supports alcohol assessment and INR/consistency counseling. Appetite, weight loss and diarrhea are intake-context questions in this qualified assessment, not a newly asserted independent INR mechanism or direction of effect.

questionReview.question: Which reasoning hazard is most important to prevent with consistent dietary vitamin K?
choices: Telling patients to avoid all green vegetables can worsen nutrition and make future reintroduction destabilizing.
Establishing a consistent vitamin K pattern with the anticoagulation service.
Checking nutritional products and supplements for vitamin K before changing intake.
Reviewing the INR and administration plan when an enteral formula or feeding schedule changes.
questionReview.rationale: The hazard is imposing total vitamin K avoidance instead of consistency. The other choices support a coordinated intake, administration and monitoring plan.
questionReview.review: Only complete green-vegetable avoidance is the hazard. The three alternatives are appropriate consistency, product reconciliation and administration/INR review actions. Nutritional inadequacy/change is a qualified inference from consistency counseling and516 nutrition-sensitive dosing, not a new numeric dietary prescription.

questionReview.question: INR falls after continuous enteral feeding begins, even though the formula contains little vitamin K. What should be assessed before repeated warfarin escalation?
choices: Escalate warfarin based only on the vitamin K amount, leaving drug-feed timing unchanged
Drug-feed timing, delivery and a coordinated feed-hold plan with INR monitoring
Keep feeds running during warfarin and use water flushing alone to prevent drug-feed binding
Change only the formula to a lower-vitamin-K product, without reviewing drug delivery or INR follow-up
questionReview.rationale: Enteral products can bind warfarin and reduce its effect; vitamin K content is a separate contributor. A low-vitamin-K formula does not exclude a drug-feed interaction. Review the actual delivery and feeding schedule, coordinate a drug-specific hold and reassess INR when feeding changes. Flushing alone does not replace the interaction plan.
questionReview.review: The local case is retained at the same ID/prompt/key/correct-answer text/anchor.170 states EN binding lowers INR separately from variable vitamin K. The new distractors focus on plausible but incomplete formula-only/dose-only/flush-only management rather than abandoning all nutrition or changing the monitoring test. A coordinated drug-specific plan with INR monitoring is the unique best answer.

teachingReview.heading: Keep vitamin K consistent
teachingReview.body: Patients do not need to eliminate green vegetables or other nutritious vitamin K sources. A stable intake can be incorporated into maintenance dosing. Major diet, appetite, supplement, enteral-feed, or weight changes require communication and closer INR monitoring.
teachingReview.review: Consistent nutrition and reassessment; preserve diet quality. For EN, separate binding fromvitaminK and coordinate the book-specific timing example with nutrition/INR follow-up.

teachingReview.heading: Coordinate warfarin with enteral nutrition
teachingReview.body: Enteral products can bind warfarin and reduce its effect. Formula vitamin K content is a separate contributor, so a low-vitamin-K formula does not exclude a feeding interaction. Review the formula, drug delivery and feeding schedule. Coordinate a warfarin-specific hold and INR follow-up with pharmacy and nutrition services, including how adequate nutrition will be delivered. The supplied review book describes holding feeds for one hour before and one hour after warfarin; this is a drug-specific example, not a hold for every medicine. Reassess the plan and INR when feeding changes or stops.
teachingReview.review: Consistent nutrition and reassessment; preserve diet quality. For EN, separate binding fromvitaminK and coordinate the book-specific timing example with nutrition/INR follow-up.
